title: Targeted retest harness and golden snapshots for config-triggered output anomalies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: After a production incident where a config flip (kv_cache=false in a canary rollout) produced systematic hallucination patterns for a high-value customer, we observed a gap between our existing eval sampling and the actual failure surface. This ticket implements a lightweight, targeted retest harness that replays the exact request vectors and configuration deltas that accompanied the incident and captures golden-reference output snapshots for future automatic comparison.

Problem statement: Current evals cover broad coverage but miss narrow, config-induced distribution shifts that manifest only under specific request sequences and cached KV state. Post-incident analysis showed we lacked the ability to: 1) persist and assert on per-request golden outputs tied to a config namespace; 2) quickly re-run prior request traces against a candidate config change; and 3) surface small but semantically meaningful regressions as actionable alerts.

Goal: Implement a reproducible retest harness and golden-snapshot datastore so that future config or model changes run an automated regression check against the exact incident playback. The harness should be lightweight, versioned, and integrated into the config rollouts pipeline so it can block unsafe changes or open a labeled investigation if thresholds are breached.
acceptance_criteria: A retest harness that can replay stored request traces with configurable environment (model, quantization, kv_cache, batcher settings) exists and runs locally and in CI
Golden snapshots (token-level and normalized text-level) are stored in a versioned datastore keyed by (model_version, config_delta_id, trace_id) and retrievable via API

A comparison runner computes token-level diffs plus semantic similarity metrics (embedding cos, n-gram overlap, and normalized hallucination signals) and returns a pass/fail with detailed diff artifacts
A gate integration for the config-rollout pipeline that can mark a change as blocked if > X% of traces fail or if any fail with 'high' hallucination signal
Documentation and runbook entry in Confluence describing how to add new traces, interpret diffs, and trigger manual investigation
Two example incident traces (from the recent customer event) are ingested and produce reproducible failures when run against the problematic config in CI
implementation_plan: Design minimal trace schema: request inputs, deterministic seed, tokenization snapshot, server-side KV snapshot id (optional), metadata (customer, route, timestamp)
Build trace ingestion pipeline (ingest CLI + small API) to persist traces to blobstore and register metadata in our config eval index
Implement retest runner service that can instantiate an ephemeral runtime container with specified model and config flags, replay the trace, and capture token stream and logits
Add golden snapshot writer that records both raw token sequence and normalized text form (strip whitespace, detokenize canonical) and computes baseline embeddings
Create comparison runner with thresholds for token-diff percent, embedding similarity, and hallucination heuristic scoring
Wire results back into rollout pipeline: update rollout job to call retest runner as a preflight step for config changes tagged 'sensitive'
Add CI job to run the two incident traces on PRs touching serving runtime, batching, KV cache logic
testing_plan: Unit tests for trace schema serialization/deserialization
Integration test: ingest a real incident trace, run in ephemeral runner, assert we reproduce the output seen in production logs
Regression test suite: three synthetic traces that exercise short, streaming, and long-context scenarios
Performance smoke: ensure harness replay for a 512-token trace completes within SLAs (target: <10s per trace on test infra)
False-positive audit: run comparison runner on historical non-incident traces to calibrate thresholds and record expected FP rate
rollout_plan: Alpha deploy: internal-only runner tied to the rollout sandbox for two weeks
Beta deploy: enable for 'sensitive' config flips and notify SRE/Oncall on any failures for review
Full deploy: integrate as optional preflight gate for all config rollouts after 2 weeks of stable ops and adjusted thresholds
Post-deploy: 1-week monitoring window where all failures create tickets with attached diffs for oncall
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-trace pass rate, mean embedding similarity, token-diff distribution
Alert: when a rollout preflight fails with 'high' hallucination score -> Sev3 to SRE + ML
Alert: if FP rate on non-incident historical traces > 5% -> notify QA to recalibrate thresholds
Audit log: every retest run persisted with links to config-delta, PR, and runtime metrics
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: storing token-level golden snapshots increases storage; we will keep full token logs for 'sensitive' traces only and compressed normalized text for others
Tradeoff: tight thresholds reduce risk but increase false positives; initial thresholds will bias towards recall (catch more regressions) and be tightened after 2 weeks
Decision: do not attempt to fully simulate multi-tenant runtime resource contention in the harness — this ticket focuses on deterministic algorithmic regressions caused by config/model diffs
Future: consider hook to run harness on live sampled prod traffic in a read-only mirror mode (separate ticket)
Privacy: redact customer PII from stored traces using the existing scrubber before persisting
comments: 2025-03-10 Maya Chen: Created ticket after postmortem. Initial scope focused on deterministic retest for config deltas. Assigned to Owen.

2025-03-11 Owen Patel: Spike completed. Prototype runner can replay a 256-token trace and reproduce token outputs locally. Found tokenization drift due to library bump — added tokenization snapshot to schema.
2025-03-13 QA (Priya Rao): Ran the two incident traces through prototype; reproduced the hallucination in both. Proposed initial embedding similarity threshold of 0.78.

2025-03-15 SRE (Luca Martínez): Suggested integrating runner with sandbox rollout job; called out infra cost for ephemeral GPU. We'll target CPU replay first with smaller models and expand to GPU for final verification.

2025-03-18 Owen Patel: PR opened for trace ingestion CLI and basic runner - link in 'links'. Next: add comparison runner and CI gating. Blocking: need storage quota increase for sensitive trace bucket (submitted request ENG-20901).
